name: Breakdown
description: The machine broke down. It was willing to run, something failed, and it made nothing until it was fixed.

name: Weld gun fault
description: A robot's weld gun faulted - no current, a stuck cylinder, a cable. The robot stops, its cell stops with it, and somebody from maintenance goes into the cell. The PLC's fault 101.

name: Robot collision stop
description: A robot's collision detection stopped it: it touched a fixture, a body or another robot. Nothing moves until a person has looked and reset it. The PLC's fault 102.

name: Tip dress
description: A welding robot dressing its electrode tips, every few hundred welds. Planned, a few seconds each, and the cell waits for it.

name: Changeover
description: The line was changing over. A planned stop: nothing is wrong and nobody is being called out.

name: Micro stop
description: A short stop of the kind that happens many times an hour - a jam, a misfeed, a reset - cleared in seconds by whoever was standing there. Nothing is broken and nothing needs reporting.

name: Starved
description: Nothing arrived for it to work on. The machine was willing and there was nothing wrong with it; the shortage was upstream.

name: Blocked
description: There was nowhere to put what it made. The machine was willing and there was nothing wrong with it; the hold-up was downstream.

name: Not yet determined
description: It stopped and nobody knows why yet. A real answer, recorded as one: a stop labelled this way is counted, can be found again and can be re-labelled, which is more than a blank box ever gave anybody.
